english: Let $P$ be the point on the parabola $y^{2}=4x$ that is nearest to the point $A(-1,14)$, and let $S$ be the focus of the parabola. Then the area of the triangle $SAP$ is
hindi: माना कि परवलय $y^{2}=4x$ पर स्थित $P$ वह बिन्दु है जो बिन्दु $A(-1,14)$ के निकटतम है, तथा $S$ परवलय की नाभि है। तब त्रिभुज $SAP$ का क्षेत्रफल है
solution: The nearest point is the foot of a normal through $A$. Normal at $(t^{2},2t)$: $y=-tx+2t+t^{3}$
$AP^{2}=f(t)=(t^{2}+1)^{2}+(2t-14)^{2}$, $f'(t)=4(t^{3}+3t-14)$ changes sign only at $t=2$, so $t=2$ gives the global minimum: $P(4,4)$
solution_full: For a point $P(t^{2},2t)$ of $y^{2}=4x$, the square of the distance from $A(-1,14)$ is $f(t)=(t^{2}+1)^{2}+(2t-14)^{2}$.

$f'(t)=4t(t^{2}+1)+4(2t-14)=4(t^{3}+3t-14)$. Equivalently, the nearest point is the foot of a normal through $A$: the normal at $(t^{2},2t)$ is $y=-tx+2t+t^{3}$, and it passes through $(-1,14)$ when $14=t+2t+t^{3}$, the same cubic.
Since $t^{3}+3t-14$ is increasing, $f'(t)<0$ for $t<2$ and $f'(t)>0$ for $t>2$; hence $f$ has its global minimum at $t=2$ and the nearest point is $P(4,4)$ (distance $\sqrt{25+100}=5\sqrt{5}$).
The focus of $y^{2}=4x$ is $S(1,0)$. With $\overrightarrow{SA}=(-2,14)$ and $\overrightarrow{SP}=(3,4)$, area of triangle $SAP=\dfrac{1}{2}|(-2)(4)-(14)(3)|=\dfrac{1}{2}|-8-42|=25$.
originality_note: New: the point is taken on the directrix, which makes the normal cubic t^3+3t-14 monotonic (a single foot, so the nearest point is forced), and the question then closes a triangle with the focus (way 5, combination of nearest point and focal geometry). Closest known: 'shortest distance from a point to y^2 = 4ax by the normal' textbook exercises. Different because: the nearest point is used to build triangle SAP, and the uniqueness of the foot has to be argued from the monotonic cubic.

concept_use.Normal to the parabola: point, slope and: The parametric normal y = -tx + 2t + t^3 is made to pass through A(-1, 14), giving t^3 + 3t - 14 = 0.
concept_use.Minimum distance of a point from a curve: The nearest point is located where the derivative of the squared distance f(t) vanishes (equivalently, along the normal), and the sign change of f' shows it is the global minimum.
